fieldValues.title: Retire Namespace Format / Schema Notation sections and their 5 orphaned subsections (RFC-042 Change B, srs#710)
fieldValues.summary: Finalized the last 2 section records and their 5 un-reparented subsection children (Convention, Reserved namespaces, Reference format, Name convention, Version semantics) under rfc-decision-1e7c0c8e by adding derived-from edges and meta.derivedFrom to the pre-existing merged mechanism successor (b3c293f9, from #691), then record delete --cascade on all 7. Fixed a real check-rfc-integration.mjs gap the deletion surfaced (no concept:/mechanism: token kind existed) rather than hand-patching around it.
fieldValues.body:
Claimed 2026-09-11T03:38:11Z from srs#710's gate:dispatched via srs#580's queue, one dispatch after PR #745 (unit-172533a1). Ground re-measured current state: 3 section records remained (Namespace Format, Schema Notation, Key Invariants) and 50 subsection records after this unit (55 before).

Unlike PR #745's 6 subsections (already migrated to standalone mechanisms, only their example-leaf children orphaned), this unit's target sections were themselves still un-retired: PR #691 had already merged both sections' full content into one mechanism ('Notational conventions', b3c293f9, contained by the 'Reading this specification' concept) and set derived-from edges from it to both sections, but never touched the two sections' own subsection children (Namespace Format had 4: Convention, Reserved namespaces, Reference format, Name convention; Schema Notation had 1: Version semantics). Verified none of the 5 had any outbound relations of their own (no further orphaned leaves beneath them) before treating them as pure dissolve-into-existing-successor cases. Confirmed by content diff that b3c293f9's prose already verbatim covered all 5 subsections' substance (namespace grammar, core reservation, canonical reference form, snake_case naming, the version-bump table) -- no new mechanism/concept needed, just provenance + deletion.

Provenance: added 5 new derived-from relations (b3c293f9 -> each subsection), then set b3c293f9.meta.derivedFrom to an array of all 7 predecessor instanceIds (2 sections + 5 subsections) via whole-object record update. No prior successor in this migration had merged more than a small number of records into meta.derivedFrom as a bare scalar; used an array since the field is an unstructured escape-bag (rfc-decision-6fc7e142/628cf6c4) with no schema constraint against it, and a scalar would have been lossy. This is a precedent future many-to-one merges in this migration should follow.

Deleted the 5 subsections and 2 sections via record delete --cascade. This left two now-empty section-typed containers behind (namespace-format-971c88d2, schema-notation-6cbfa40e) -- record delete --cascade clears a container's memberInstanceIds/rootInstanceIds when its members/root are deleted but does not delete the container itself. Deleted both explicitly via srs container delete; confirmed via grep that no other file referenced either containerId first.

Key finding (see finding record, contains edge below): check-rfc-integration.mjs's manifest-token resolver only recognized `section:<slug>`/`subsection:<slug>` tokens, indexed only from live com.semanticops.spec/section and /subsection records. Deleting Version semantics broke RFC-030's `subsection:version-semantics` token -- caught immediately by validate-all (not silently). Rather than hand-patch just RFC-030's token to something that happened to already resolve, extended the checker with `concept:<slug>`/`mechanism:<slug>` resolution mirroring the existing pattern exactly (same slugify, same indexing loop, same fail-message list), since this is a mechanical, load-bearing consequence of RFC-042 Change B itself and will recur for every remaining RFC citation of a subsection this migration has yet to retire. Documented the two new token kinds in CLAUDE.md. Proved the new resolver actually rejects bad input (not a rubber-stamp): temporarily pointed RFC-030's token at `mechanism:does-not-exist-anywhere`, confirmed check-rfc-integration.mjs failed with the expected message, then reverted.

Cleared 2 now-stale scripts/spec-coherence-allowlist.json entries and 7 now-stale scripts/publication-reachability-exclusions.json entries that existed only because these 7 records hadn't been deleted yet -- shrink discipline, not new suppression.

Both gates verified green by direct exit code from a background run (not a piped tail, which silently discards node's real exit status -- this bit me once mid-unit: my first validate-all run was piped through `| tail -30` and read as exit 0 despite validate-all itself printing 'Some validations failed'; re-ran without the pipe to get the true signal). node scripts/validate-all.mjs and node scripts/check-release-drift.mjs both exit 0 on the final state. part-container-membership.mjs --check: zero drift (these 7 records were never Part-container members, so no reparenting of Part membership was needed here, unlike PR #745). Re-rendered with the pinned CLI: only docs/spec/rfcs/rfc-catalog.md changed (RFC-030's updated citation text); no other rendered output changed since these records were never in any Part container's rendered subtree.

Remaining for srs#710: Key Invariants (no successor yet, blocked on scripts/lib/invariant-region.mjs redesign, carried-context-31ea3659), 50 more subsection records (carried-context-87e8e448's orphaned-example-leaf check still applies to each), then the final srs type delete PR once both section/subsection counts hit zero. New for the next worker: before deleting any section/subsection record, grep srs/records/tier-2/rfc-*.json for `section:<old-title-slug>`/`subsection:<old-title-slug>` manifest tokens citing it, and update them to concept:/mechanism: (now supported) pointing at the actual successor -- otherwise validate-all catches it after the fact rather than the unit anticipating it (see carried_context record, contains edge below).

PR: https://github.com/the-greenman/srs/pull/747, gate:auto-merge armed (SQUASH). Stopping per the merge-rights contract.
